name: Laryngotracheoesophageal cleft

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and endoscopic diagnostic criteria for laryngotracheoesophageal cleft

criteria.description: Direct visualization of the cleft extending from the larynx into the trachea and/or esophagus via endoscopy
Presence of respiratory distress, aspiration, or recurrent pneumonia in neonates or infants
Imaging studies (e.g., contrast esophagogram) demonstrating abnormal communication between airway and esophagus
Identification of associated congenital anomalies such as tracheoesophageal fistula or cardiac defects

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Endoscopic visualization of the cleft plus clinical respiratory symptoms or radiologic evidence of abnormal communication
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily confirmed by endoscopic examination; imaging and clinical presentation support diagnosis.

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers during aspiration pneumonia episodes
imaging: Contrast esophagogram showing abnormal communication between larynx/trachea and esophagus
Chest X-ray revealing recurrent infiltrates or aspiration pneumonia
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be associated with syndromes such as Opitz G/BBB syndrome
other: Endoscopic visualization of cleft extending from larynx into trachea and/or esophagus

distinguishingFeatures: Usually diagnosed by inability to pass nasogastric tube
Membranous tissue partially obstructing the laryngeal inlet
No communication with esophagus or trachea
Typically presents with hoarseness and stridor without aspiration

redFlags: Recurrent aspiration pneumonia despite standard care
Failure to thrive with feeding difficulties
references: Kamel KS, et al. Laryngotracheoesophageal cleft: diagnosis and management. Int J Pediatr Otorhinolaryngol. 2017.
Holinger LD. Laryngotracheoesophageal clefts. Ann Otol Rhinol Laryngol. 1989.
